newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions talk to gov't on labor law - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions talk to gov't on labor law - report.

text.p: Rodolfo Daer, head of Argentina's labor federation (CGT), met Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa to restart talks on controversial laws to change working conditions, the private DyN news agency said Thursday.

Contact between unions and the government to agree on a package of labor laws being sponsored by President Carlos Menem had broken down and the CGT held a 24-hour general strike in August and a 36-hour strike in September.

Menem hopes the package of laws including measures to end collective wage talks across industries and to replace compensation payments for dismissal with unemployment insurance will cut Argentina's 17.1-percent joblessness rate.
But Congress has been reluctant to pass the package and the president has threatened to impose the measures by decree.
